questions.q: What problem does this lesson say an unmonitored pipeline repeats from Chapter 5?
options: The database being unsecured
A real mechanism existing, but someone still having to notice when it stops working — the same shape of problem Chapter 5 solved for the database itself
The failover group not being tested
The Bicep template being hardcoded
questions.explain: A failed pipeline run that nobody notices is the same category of gap Chapter 5's health checks and alerting closed for the database.

questions.q: What does Data Factory's Monitor hub actually show for a pipeline run?
options: Only whether the pipeline exists
Status (Succeeded/Failed/In Progress), start and end time, and for a failed run, the specific activity and error that caused it
Only billing cost information
Only the source file's size
questions.explain: The Monitor hub is the first place to look after a reported failure to understand exactly what went wrong.

questions.q: What does the alert rule example in this lesson actually trigger on, and where does it route?
options: Any pipeline run at all, routed to a public dashboard
A pipeline run status of Failed, routed to the same on-call DBA distribution Lesson 19's health-check alerts already use
A successful run, routed to leadership
A schema change, routed to the Data Factory admin only
questions.explain: Using the same notification path as Lesson 19 means Overlook's on-call DBA gets one consistent alerting channel instead of several disconnected ones.

questions.q: Why does an alert on pipeline failure still matter even though the Copy activity has a retry policy?
options: Retry policies make alerts entirely unnecessary
A retry policy only handles transient failures automatically — by the time an alert actually fires, a simple retry has already been ruled out, so the alert specifically means something real
Retry policies and alerts are unrelated features
Alerts are only needed if retries are disabled
questions.explain: Retries catch brief, transient issues; the alert is the escalation path for failures that retries couldn't resolve on their own.

questions.q: What does Chapter 6's completion mean for the overall capstone, according to this lesson?
options: Only the Data Factory piece is done; the rest of the capstone is unrelated
All five of Lesson 2's planned pieces — infrastructure, security, HA/DR, automation, and ETL — are now complete, setting up Chapter 7's test of the whole platform under pressure
The capstone is finished and Chapter 7 is optional
Chapter 6 must be rebuilt before Chapter 7 can start
questions.explain: This closes Lesson 2's full dependency chain, which Chapter 7 then tests together under real pressure.
